input.quote: a. IBM will specify Materials to be delivered to Customer. IBM will identify them as being "Type I Materials," "Type II Materials," or otherwise as Customer and IBM agree in writing. If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7.0 defaults all Materials (deliverables) to Type II, i.e. IBM or third parties hold all right, title and interest, so work product created for us during the Service performance period is vendor-owned unless separately negotiated. The licence back for Type II Materials is limited to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform and distribute "within Customer's Enterprise only" — it carries no right to modify/prepare derivative works and no right to sublicense, so it fails the fallback position (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business) as well as the preferred position. There is also no affirmative statement that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components (Content is defined as customer-provided and Required Consents assumes third-party owners, but ownership is never confirmed). No assignment of our IP or data to IBM is created, so this is not walk-away territory. Redline flips the default to Type I (Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to include modification and sublicensing for our business, and adds a Customer Content/Customer Components ownership sentence; IBM's ownership of its pre-existing Materials and Base Components is left intact.

proposal.summary: Default Materials to Customer-owned Type I, broaden the Type II licence-back to include modification and sublicensing, and confirm Customer ownership of Content and Customer Components.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our playbook requires that we own the deliverables created for us, so we have made Type I (Customer-owned) the default where Materials are not otherwise specified, and confirmed that we retain all rights in our Content and Customer Components. Where IBM retains ownership of pre-existing Type II Materials, we need a perpetual licence that includes the right to modify and sublicense for our business purposes; retaining IBM ownership of its platform and generic tools is acceptable.

ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, prepare derivative works based on, and distribute copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business purposes, and to sublicense these rights to its Affiliates, Subcontractors and Services Recipients.

ops.text: e. Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content and the Customer Components. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content or the Customer Components, and IBM obtains no rights in them other than the limited rights expressly granted in this Agreement for the purpose of performing the Services.
